newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao to appear in court on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao to appear in court on Wednesday.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao will appear in court on Wednesday to face forgery charges in a seven-year-old criminal case, his lawyer said on Tuesday.
R.K. Anand told Reuters that Rao would appear at a hearing set for 10 a.m. (0430 GMT) in a special, high security court room in an international conference centre in the Indian capital.

"I am bringing him," Anand told Reuters by telephone. Anand said his team would press chief metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar to extend the temporary bail that has protected Rao from arrest but which expires on November 6.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, charged Rao and three others on September 26 in the case involving an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, an opposition leader who later became prime minister.
Rao, who would be the first former or acting prime minister to appear in court to face criminal charges, has not commented publicly on the case.

Rao, who stepped down as Congress party leader in September, has been named but not formally charged in a separate criminal cheating case. Rao has said he is innocent in the cheating case. Both the forgery and cheating cases carry maximum penalties of seven years in prison.
